notes: The source gives the same 0.298 leading time coefficient for arbitrary and ideal lattices. For suitable cyclotomic ideal lattices, rotational symmetry yields linear-factor improvements in both time and space. These polynomial gains are not a smaller exponential coefficient. The selected ring and embedding must be specified for concrete comparisons. Theorem 1 gives 0.2972, often rounded to 0.298 in the abstract; this is a precision normalization, not a new algorithmic improvement.
